# Paired tails at the TRUE Minkowski centroid: a linear obstruction and two corrections

Let d>=1, let A,B be d-dimensional convex bodies of the same volume a>0, and put M=(A+B)/2, m=|M|, y=g_M. Define the actual paired-tail infimum

    P(A,B;y)=inf_(u!=0,t in R)
      [|A intersect {u.x>=u.y+t}|+|B intersect {u.x>=u.y-t}|].         (1)

The proposed inequality P>=2 Gamma_d(2a-m)_+, with Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d, is FALSE already in d=2. More strongly, no finite constant C can give

    P(A,B;g_M)>=2 Gamma_2 a-C(m-a)                                   (2)

for all equal-area planar convex bodies. This statement uses the TRUE centroid of M, not the average of the two original centroids. The archived trapezoid obstruction for the latter point is adapted below with its centroid displacement tracked exactly.

## 1. Exact rational equal-area bodies and their midpoint centroid

For w>1 define

    h(w)=(w+w^(-1))/2, ell(w)=(w-w^(-1))/2,
    K_w={ (x,z):ell(w)<=x<=h(w), |z|<=x/2 }.

These are full-dimensional compact convex trapezoids, with rational vertices when w is rational. Their vertical section length is x, so

    |K_w|=1/2, g_(K_w)=(mu(w),0), mu(w)=w/2+1/(6w^3).               (3)

For A=K_u, B=K_v, their actual Minkowski average is exactly the same cone strip with lower and upper x coordinates

    L=[ell(u)+ell(v)]/2, H=[h(u)+h(v)]/2.

For each feasible sum of x coordinates, the summed section intervals have length equal to that sum, which proves both set inclusions. Its area and TRUE centroid coordinate are

    m=(u+v)^2/(8uv),
    g=(u+v)(3u^2v^2+1)/(12u^2v^2).                                  (4)

Indeed m=(H^2-L^2)/2 and g=(H^3-L^3)/(3m). Direct subtraction gives

    g-[mu(u)+mu(v)]/2=-(u-v)^2(u+v)/(12u^3v^3).                      (5)

This offset is negative and is not discarded.

Take the specific rational values

    v=101/100, u=5051/5000.

In (1) use u_direction=(1,0) and shift t=h(u)-g. The A threshold is exactly h(u), so its closed supporting-edge cap has area zero. The B threshold is

    tau=2g-h(u)=17358032822901/52050808560200.

It is strictly proper: its exact distances from the lower and upper support levels of B are

    tau-ell(v)=84200507550/260254042801>0,
    h(v)-tau=173476762550/260254042801>0.

Thus the paired area equals (h(v)^2-tau^2)/2. Here

    m=102030201/204060400,
    2m-1=1/102030200,

and exact rational subtraction gives

    (8/9)(1-m)-(h(v)^2-tau^2)/2
       =13214404325059960523/60958950114838265933040900>0.            (6)

Since a=1/2 and 2 Gamma_2=8/9, the first term in (6) is exactly the proposed positive right side 2 Gamma_2(2a-m). A single actual cap pair below it disproves the infimum bound. Every area and point is actual; no numerical optimizer or approximation is used. The supporting-edge boundary has zero area, while the other cut is strictly proper.

## 2. An exact positive polynomial rules out every finite linear payment

For rational 0<s<=1/100 put

    v=1+s, u=1+s+2s^2,
    tau=2g-h(u).

Both selected caps have the same statuses as above. One quick exact verification of properness is as follows. Put mu(w)=w/2+1/(6w^3), L0(w)=h(w)-mu(w), and tau_old=mu(v)+mu(u)-h(u). Since L0 is decreasing for w>1,

    tau_old>=2mu(v)-h(v)>=1/3,

where the last function equals 1/3 at w=1 and has derivative
(w^2-1)(w^2+2)/(2w^4)>=0. Also tau_old<mu(v)<1<=h(v). By (5),

    Dg=[mu(u)+mu(v)]/2-g
       =s^4(u+v)/(3u^3v^3)<s^4,
    tau=tau_old-2Dg.

Thus tau>=1/3-2s^4>s>=ell(v), and tau<h(v). The A cap remains its supporting edge of zero area.

Direct rational algebra in (3)--(4) now gives two exact identities:

    m-a=s^4/[2(1+s)(1+s+2s^2)],

    2 Gamma_2 a - (h(v)^2-tau^2)/2
      =s^3 P(s)/[18(1+s)^4(1+s+2s^2)^4],                           (7)

where

    P(s)=4+30s+132s^2+374s^3+735s^4+1035s^5
               +1033s^6+710s^7+300s^8+56s^9.

Every coefficient is positive. These are identities of rational functions, verified by bringing the displayed formulas to a common denominator; no asymptotic approximation is needed for their signs. In particular the raw deficit is positive for every displayed s. Dividing the two identities yields

    [2 Gamma_2 a-pairedcap]/(m-a)
       =P(s)/[9s(1+s)^3(1+s+2s^2)^3]
       >=4/[9s(101/100)^3(51/50)^3],                              (8)

which diverges as rational s decreases to zero. Hence (2) fails for every finite C. This also confirms the exact leading orders

    m-a=(1/2)s^4+O(s^5),
    2 Gamma_2 a-pairedcap=(2/9)s^3+O(s^4).

More generally, (7) and the bounded positive denominator imply that no finite constant times (m-a)^alpha can compensate the deficit when alpha>3/4. The ratio has a lower bound proportional to s^(3-4alpha), which diverges. This identifies a necessary restriction on any power modulus; it does NOT claim sufficiency at exponent 3/4.

The centroid mismatch is not the cause of the failure. Changing from the average original centroid to g_M lowers the B threshold from tau_old to tau, which makes the selected paired cost LARGER, by exactly [tau_old^2-tau^2]/2>0. Nevertheless the positive shape deficit (7) remains. Independent opposite translations can make the two original centroids coincide at their average; they leave M fixed and merely reparameterize the paired shift t. Thus that version has the same defect, with its true midpoint centroid retained.

## 3. A universal volume-only replacement

For arbitrary d>=1, the following weaker, fully explicit statement IS true:

    P(A,B;g_M) >=
      a [1-{2[(1-Gamma_d)m/a]^(1/d)-1}^d]_+.                        (9)

The expression inside braces is nonnegative because m>=a by Brunn--Minkowski and Gamma_d<=1/2. In particular (9) is positive whenever

    m<a/(1-Gamma_d).

Proof. Fix an actual pair of halfspaces in (1), and let their captured volumes be U,V. If U+V>=a, (9) is immediate because its right side is at most a. Otherwise put q=a-U-V>0. Both complementary truncated bodies have positive volume, and their midpoint lies in the residual halfspace {u.x<=u.g_M} of M. Ordinary Grünbaum applied to the opposite closed centroid halfspace of M bounds that residual volume above by (1-Gamma_d)m. Brunn--Minkowski therefore gives

    (a-U)^(1/d)+(a-V)^(1/d)
               <=2[(1-Gamma_d)m]^(1/d).                              (10)

Among two numbers in [0,a] with sum a+q, the sum of their 1/d powers is minimized at the endpoints a,q, by concavity of the power function. Thus the left side of (10) is at least a^(1/d)+q^(1/d). Rearranging gives

    q<=[2((1-Gamma_d)m)^(1/d)-a^(1/d)]^d,

which is exactly (9), including the zero truncation. All hyperplane boundaries are null for these full-dimensional bodies; using closed complementary cuts changes no volume and their actual midpoint inclusion is valid.

For d=1, equal-length intervals have m=a and the formula gives a, which is the exact paired cost. In d=2 at m=a the lower constant in (9) is (12sqrt(5)-20)/9, strictly below the sharp same-body value 8/9. The loss in this corrected statement is explicit; it is not presented as a sharp or small-deficit-stable replacement.

## 4. A shape-sensitive replacement retaining the sharp same-body constant

There is also a corrected bound which retains 2 Gamma_d a at zero actual shape mismatch. Put

    K=g_M+(a/m)^(1/d)(M-g_M),

so K is a convex body of volume a and centroid g_M. Define the ACTUAL aligned symmetric-difference error

    E(A,B;M)=min_(h in R^d)
       [ |(A-h) triangle K|+|(B+h) triangle K| ]/2,                  (11)

where triangle denotes symmetric difference. Then

    P(A,B;g_M)>= [2 Gamma_d a-E(A,B;M)]_+.                           (12)

This invokes the already proved ordinary same-body paired-tail theorem in `candidate 732b11a769399016`: for one convex body K and its centroid g_K, its two oppositely shifted tails sum to at least 2 Gamma_d|K| for every direction and shift. This is an ordinary continuous theorem, independently audited in `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`, and does not invoke OC or any two-body compensation statement.

To prove (12), fix h. Opposite translations A-h,B+h leave M unchanged and leave the all-shift infimum (1) unchanged: for a fixed direction they merely replace t by t+u.h. For each halfspace H,

    |(A-h) intersect H|>=|K intersect H|-|K minus (A-h)|,

and similarly for B+h. Since all three bodies have volume a, each loss on the right is half the corresponding symmetric difference. Apply these comparisons to the paired halfspaces, then the same-body paired theorem to K, and finally minimize the two actual shape errors over h. The infimum is a minimum: translation is continuous in L^1 for bounded convex bodies, and outside a sufficiently large ball both translated bodies are disjoint from K, where the error is the constant 2a. Hence a minimizer exists on a compact ball (or the constant value is attained outside it).

Formula (12) preserves the sharp same-body constant and separately displays the actual shape information that a linear function of m-a cannot control sufficiently. No estimate of E by a linear Minkowski-volume excess is asserted; the exact counterexample above precludes using such a payment to restore (2).
